story.head: The Stars are on a heater
paras: The Blues won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-0 in Dallas on Oct 2. The Blues have won two in a row, and the Stars have won four straight. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Stars second (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Blues seventh (18th).
The Stars’ record (.682) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.602), largely because they’re 8-4 in one-goal games. The Blues’ record (.545) is about what their chances are worth.

This season, the Stars have outscored teams 62-54, even though they’ve been outscored 40-39 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 13-9, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). Dallas has allowed 2.45 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Blues, they ice the puck less than anyone (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and take a lot of high-quality shots (3rd). The Stars’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Blues. On top of that, the Stars’ power play bites, but the Blues’ doesn’t.

Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, with six goals in nine games against St. Louis since 2023-24. Jason Robertson (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jimmy Snuggerud (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Jake Oettinger (12-4-1 / .901 SV% in 17 GS) is in line to start for Dallas. Joel Hofer (9-6-1 / .923 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and will likely start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Dvorský, Suter and Toropchenko out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Kiviranta, Faksa and Perron.
